hints: Remember an ester splits into two parts, the alkanoate part comes from the acid and the alkyl part comes from the alcohol.
Check the acid part first. Acids with 4 or more carbons can branch to form chain isomers, so which acids in the options are too long to have no chain isomers?
For the remaining alcohols, count how many positions the OH can occupy on a straight chain. A 4-carbon alcohol has two positions while a 5-carbon alcohol has three.
walkthrough:
**Split the ester into acid + alcohol**

Esterification is acid + alcohol to give alkyl alkanoate + water. The second word tells you the acid, the first word tells you the alcohol.

$$\text{alkyl alkanoate from } \text{alkanol + alkanoic acid}$$

**Use the acid clue to narrow down**

P has no possible chain isomers. Methanoic, ethanoic and propanoic acids ($C_1$ to $C_3$) cannot branch, but butanoic acid ($C_4$) can form $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ and $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCOOH}$, and pentanoic acid branches even more. So P must be ethanoate or propanoate. This leaves only butyl propanoate and pentyl ethanoate.

**Use the alcohol clue to decide**

Q has only one positional isomer, meaning there are two possible positions in total for the OH group. Butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol are the only two straight chain positions, so butanol fits perfectly. Pentan-1-ol, pentan-2-ol and pentan-3-ol give two extra isomers, so pentanol has too many. Therefore the only possible combination is butanol + propanoic acid, which is butyl propanoate.

options.A: Acid part is propanoate from propanoic acid, $C_3$, which cannot form a branched chain isomer. Alcohol part is butyl from butanol, $C_4$, which has exactly two straight-chain positions, butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol, so it has only one other positional isomer. Both conditions are met.
options.B: Acid part is butanoate from butanoic acid, $C_4$. This does have a chain isomer, 2-methylpropanoic acid, so it fails the P condition even though ethyl alcohol has only one form.
options.C: Acid part is ethanoate from ethanoic acid, $C_2$, which correctly has no chain isomers. However the alcohol part is pentyl from pentanol, $C_5$, which has three positions, pentan-1-ol, pentan-2-ol and pentan-3-ol, so it has two positional isomers, not one.
options.D: Acid part is pentanoate from pentanoic acid, $C_5$, which has several branched chain isomers, so it fails the P condition. Alcohol part is propyl from propanol which does fit the alcohol condition, but both parts must fit.
